// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x413660 HudUiMgr::SwitchActiveDialog (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source file: D:\Proj\Battlesport\hud.cpp
// BN limitation: HLIL visually places HudUiMgr::DisableHud after the disabled-case assignment, but assembly branches around it, so DisableHud belongs only to the was-enabled path. // -- end xref --
0x412db0 void __thiscall HudUiMgr::SwitchActiveDialog(struct HudLayoutBase* newDialog)
{

        g_HudUiMgr.layoutDelayFrames = 2
    else

//
// Transforms modal probe points through the player motion basis, builds candidate hits, selects per-sample heights, and fills the impact histogram plus attachment outputs.
//
// The owning modal object for this helper is `primaryModalState = self->primaryModalState`; `masterModalData = primaryModalState->masterModalData`. //
// The per-frame probe Y offset is `probeYAdvance`, and the candidate selector receives a clamped rise window of `min(4.0f, 1.0f - probeYAdvance)` for geometric-height selection. // Physical source block: src/Battlesport/player.cpp [0x41ea90,0x42de10); block-order evidence only.
// Copies direction, transforms it by the player's root-node rotation, then applies pitch/roll angle impulse and local X/Z velocity impulse using the two stack scale factors. BN still renders the scalar math with x87 fconvert casts.

0x427a20 void __fastcall Player::ApplyPitchRollVelocityImpulseFromDirection(struct zUtil_SaveGameState* saveState, struct zVec3* direction, float angleScale, float velocityScale)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x42e330 RecoilApp::InitializeDisplay (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Physical source-file block: src/Battlesport/RecoilApp.cpp [0x42de10,0x436630), layer recoilapp_engine_startup_state_machine_layer [0x42e220,0x42f9f0). Initializes video/display state from options. BN caveat from assembly remains: checked SpanOcclusionInit error path is folded in HLIL because the callee currently returns constant 0.
// -- end xref --
0x42c520 int32_t __fastcall RecoilApp::InitializeDisplay(HWND hWnd)
{
    enum zVidModeIndex modeIndex = zVid::GetVideoModeIndexFromOptions()
    int32_t fullscreen = zOpt::GetFullscreenOption()

    if (zVideo::InitVideoSystem(hWnd, zVid::GetHwApiOption(), fullscreen, modeIndex) != ZVIDEO_STATUS_OK)
        printf("Error opening video... ABORTING RUN\n")
        fflush(&_iob[1])
        return 0

    if (zVid::GetAccelerationOption() == ZVID_HW_MODE_SOFTWARE)
        zRndr::SpanOcclusionInit(zOpt::GetWindowSectionHeight())

    int32_t pitchBytes = zVideo::GetPrimarySurfacePitch()
    int32_t bitsPerPixel = zOpt::GetDisplaySectionBitsPerPixel()
    struct zOpt_ViewRectSection* activeRegionRect = zOpt::GetDisplaySection()
    zRndr::SetFrameBufferRegion(zVideo::GetPrimarySurfacePixels(), activeRegionRect, bitsPerPixel, pitchBytes)
    zRndr::SetVideoStrideMirrors(zOpt::GetVideoStrideValue())
    zVid::InitFrameScratchBuffers()
    enum zVideoClearScreenBufferState enable = zVideo::ExchangeClearScreenBufferEnabled(ZVIDEO_CLEAR_SCREEN_BUFFER_ENABLED)
    zVideo::CallClearSwSurfaceAndZBuffer(nullptr, nullptr)
    zVideo::CallClearPrimarySurfaceAndZBuffer(nullptr)
    zVideo::AdjustSurfacesIfEnabled(nullptr, nullptr, 1, 1)
    zVideo::CallClearPrimarySurfaceAndZBuffer(nullptr)
    zVideo::AdjustSurfacesIfEnabled(nullptr, nullptr, 1, 1)
    zVideo::ExchangeClearScreenBufferEnabled(enable)
    return 1
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x42e430 RecoilApp::ShutdownEngine (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Physical source-file block: src/Battlesport/RecoilApp.cpp [0x42de10,0x436630), layer recoilapp_engine_startup_state_machine_layer [0x42e220,0x42f9f0). Engine shutdown path; subsystem callees are dependencies inside the app-state lifecycle.
// -- end xref --
0x42c620 void __thiscall RecoilApp::ShutdownEngine(struct RecoilApp* self)
{
    if (zSnd::GetCDAudioOption() != ZSND_CDAUDIO_DISABLED)
        zSndCd::Stop()

    zTurret_System::Shutdown()
    zDEClient::ShutdownGlobals()

    if (zVid::GetAccelerationOption() == ZVID_HW_MODE_SOFTWARE)
        zRndr::SpanOcclusionShutdown()

    zInput_BindMapContext::DestroyGlobal()
    HudUiMgr::ShutdownResources()

    if (zOpt::GetNetworkEnabled() != ZOPT_NETWORK_OPTION_DISABLED)
        zNetwork::ShutdownSessionRuntime()

    RecoilApp::ShutdownSubsystems(self)
    zVideo::ShutdownVideoSystem()

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x463320 CZFMVActionImage::Update (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zFMV\fmv_script.cpp
//
// Action vftable Update hook: blits the cached image to the renderer's primary target on each polled tick.
//
// Iteration count (in EDI): always 1 except when the renderer is software AND g_zVideo_RendererType (@ 0x56bbe8) != ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_SOFTWARE — in that case the loop runs twice (front+back buffer chain). Initial: edi := setne(g_RendererType != 0) + 1 → 1 in software, 2 in hardware paths.
//
// Early exit: if self->image @ +0x0c is NULL (Begin failed to load), bail out immediately and return 0.
//
// Per-iteration body:
//   1. If self->forcePrimaryPostprocess @ +0x14 != 0 OR g_zVideo_RendererType == ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_3DFX (==2):
//        zVideo_buff_RunPostprocessOnPrimaryBuffer()                                        -- runs the FxPass3 postprocess
//        zVideo_Image_BlitToActiveTarget(self->image, blitRect.x, blitRect.y, 0, NULL)     -- arg order: (image, dstX, dstY, mode, palette?)
//        zVideo_Dispatch_UnlockPrimarySurfaceState()                                        -- unlock after the blit
//      Else (software path with no postprocess):
//        g_zVideo_pfnBltSwToPrimaryRect(self->image, 0, NULL, &self->blitRect)             -- direct sw blit (no lock/unlock)
//   2. If self->doAdjustSurfaces @ +0x10 != 0:
//        zVideo_AdjustSurfacesIfEnabled(1, 1)                                               -- waitForPresent=1, blitPrimaryToSwFirst=1
//
// Return 0 always (image actions complete in one pump from the dispatcher's perspective; dispatcher relies on the script-level scheduler for advance).
//
// Calling convention: __thiscall, ECX = self, single qword stack arg (double currentTimeSec, ignored). `retn 8` reclaims it.
// -- end xref --
0x45c0c0 int32_t __thiscall CZFMVActionImage::Update(struct CZFMVActionImage* self, double currentTimeSec)
{
    int32_t eax = 0
    eax.b = g_zVideo_ActiveRendererPath != ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_SOFTWARE
    int32_t i_1 = eax + 1

    if (self->image != 0)
        int32_t i

        do
            if (self->forcePrimaryPostprocess != 0 || g_zVideo_ActiveRendererPath == ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_3DFX)
                zVideo::RunPostprocessOnPrimaryBuffer()
                zVid_Image::BlitToActiveTarget(self->image, self->blitRect.x, self->blitRect.y, 0, nullptr)
                zVideo::DispatchUnlockPrimarySurfaceState()
            else
                g_zVideo_pfnBltSwToPrimaryRect(self->image, 0, nullptr, &self->blitRect)

            if (self->doAdjustSurfaces != 0)
                zVideo::AdjustSurfacesIfEnabled(nullptr, nullptr, 1, 1)

            i = i_1
            i_1 -= 1
        while (i != 1)

    return 0
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x463440 CZFMVActionFade::Update (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zVideo\fmv_script.cpp. FMV fade per-frame update; returns 1 while fade is still in progress and 0 after clamp/completion.
//
// ABI: int32_t __thiscall zFMV_ActionFade_Update(zFMV_ActionFade* self, double currentTimeSec), retn 8. ECX=self; EAX returns the in-progress flag.
//

//

// -- end xref --
0x45c1e0 int32_t __thiscall CZFMVActionFade::Update(struct CZFMVActionFade* self, double currentTimeSec)

        return 0

    int32_t result = 1

    if (self->fadeDirectionSign s>= 0)

        x87_r7_2 - temp1_1

            currentTimeSec:4.d = 0x3ff00000
            result = 0

        currentTimeSec = x87_r7_3
        long double temp2_1 = 0.0
        x87_r7_3 - temp2_1

        if ((((x87_r7_3 < temp2_1 ? 1 : 0) << 8 | (is_unordered.t(x87_r7_3, temp2_1) ? 1 : 0) << 0xa | (x87_r7_3 == temp2_1 ? 1 : 0) << 0xe):1.b & 0x41) != 0)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x463570 CZFMVActionPlayAvi::Constructor (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Constructor for the FMV "play AVI" action. Builds the joined media path and resolves it through the CD-tree fallback. SEH-protected by handler thunk @ 0x4caf68 (Cookie -1) so partial allocations unwind cleanly. Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zVideo\fmv_script.cpp.
//
// Calling convention: __thiscall + 3 stack args (retn 0xc). ECX=self.
//   arg1 mediaRootPath (char const*)
//   arg2 mediaFileName (char const*)
//   arg3 modeFlags     (int32_t)
//
// Field map (struct zFMV_ActionPlayAvi):
//   +0    vftable    -> g_zFMV_ActionPlayAvi_Vtable @ 0x4d25c8
//   +4    next       (set NULL; appended later by zFMV_Script_AppendAction)
//   +8    mediaPath  (char*, calloc'd in this ctor)
//   +0xc  modeFlags  (int32_t; passed-through)
//
// Sequence:
// 1. self->vftable = 0x4d25c8; self->next = NULL.
// 2. rootLen = strlen(mediaRootPath); fileLen = strlen(mediaFileName)  -- both via repne scasb (not.d(ecx) - 1 idiom).
// 3. mediaPath = calloc(rootLen + fileLen + 0x1b, 1) and store at self+8. The 0x1b slack covers the literal "\\" byte, NUL terminator, and headroom for a swap by zSys_FindFileOnDriveType which can replace the buffer contents with a longer absolute path.
// 4. sprintf(mediaPath, "%s\\%s" @ 0x4dd484, mediaRootPath, mediaFileName) -- joined path written in place.
// 5. self->modeFlags = modeFlags.
// 6. _stat(mediaPath, &local_statbuf): if returns 0 (file exists at the joined relative path), DONE.
// 7. Else (_stat returns -1): mediaPath = zSys_FindFileOnDriveType(driveType=5 /* DRIVE_CDROM */, mediaPath). If a hit comes back, copy the returned absolute path INTO the existing buffer in-place (rep movsd + rep movsb of strlen+1 bytes). The pre-allocated 0x1b slack guarantees room for the typical CD root prefix.
// 8. Restore SEH and return self in EAX.
//
// Note: there is no out-of-memory check on calloc, no bounds check on the in-place copy, and no error reporting -- the call sites assume the file is locatable on the configured drive set.
// -- end xref --

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4643a0 zFMV_Stream::ReadAndDecodeFrame (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Original file: GameZRecoil/zFMV/fmv_stream.cpp
// Per-tick driver of zFMV_Stream playback: optionally seeks, decodes one video frame, and pumps the double-buffered audio refill state machine. Returns the post-advance currentFrameIndex (or 0 on AVI / decoder error).
// 1. If frameIndex != 0xFFFFFFFF, override self->currentFrameIndex with frameIndex (caller-driven seek).
// 2. If currentFrameIndex >= aviVideoFrameCount: skip read+decode, fall through to step 4 (loop bookkeeping only).
// 3. Decode pipeline:

//       → on failure log "Cannot Read AVI Video Stream" (zerr line 0x105) and return 0.
//    b. EnterCriticalSection(&self->audioLock).
//    c. ICDecompress(decompressor, 0, aviVideoFormatSrc, aviCompressedFrameBuffer, aviVideoFormatDst, imagePixels)
//       → on failure log "Cannot Decompress AVI Video Stream" (line 0x10c) and return 0 — BUG: returns while still holding audioLock (no LeaveCriticalSection on error path).
//    d. LeaveCriticalSection(&self->audioLock).
// 4. ++currentFrameIndex; wrap to 0 when it reaches aviVideoFrameCount (looping playback).
// 5. Audio pump (only when self->hasAudioTrack != 0):
//    a. If audioPlaybackStartPending != 0: zSndSample_PlayA3DSimple(audioSample) with gain=1.0f (literal 0x3f800000 pushed), clear pending, return currentFrameIndex (the rest of the audio block is skipped this tick — giving DirectSound one tick to actually start before refill begins).
//    b. Else if modeFlags != 0: classic ping-pong refill — keep the half NOT currently under the play cursor full of fresh PCM:
//       - audioRefillSecondHalfNext == 0 (we last filled second half / will fill SECOND next): when cursor entered second half (cursor > audioSegmentBytes), refill FIRST half via zFMV_Stream_FillAudioBuffer(self, offset=0, size=audioSegmentBytes) and set flag := 1.
//       - audioRefillSecondHalfNext != 0 (will fill FIRST next... NO, naming is "second-next"): when cursor returned to first half (0 < cursor < audioSegmentBytes), refill SECOND half via zFMV_Stream_FillAudioBuffer(self, offset=audioSegmentBytes, size=audioSegmentBytes) and clear flag := 0.
//       Net cycle: cursor→2nd half ⇒ refill 1st & flag:=1 ⇒ cursor→1st half ⇒ refill 2nd & flag:=0 ⇒ repeat.
// 6. Return self->currentFrameIndex.
// -- end xref --

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x46c5b0 zGeometry_Vec3Array::ReversePoints (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Reverses the tail of a zVec3 polygon point list in place, preserving points[0] as the anchor.
//
// Given `points[0..pointCount-1]`, the function produces `points[0], points[pointCount-1], points[pointCount-2], ..., points[1]` — i.e. it flips the winding order of a polygon without rotating the starting vertex.
//
// Algorithm (floor(pointCount/2) iterations):
//   front = &points[1];
//   back  = &points[pointCount - 1];

//       *back-- = *front;
//       *front++ = tmp;
//   }
//
// For pointCount in {0,1,2,3} the loop runs 0, 0, 1, 1 times respectively (pointCount=2 is a degenerate quad-swap that hits self-swap at the one iteration when back==front). For even pointCount the final iteration is back==front == middle+1 and performs a harmless self-copy.
//
// Sole caller: `zGeometry_Vec3Array::EnsurePositiveCrossZ` (0x46c620) uses this to flip a polygon from CW to CCW when the computed cross-product Z of the first triangle is ≤ 0.
//

//
// EXHAUSTION CHECKLIST (for crit 11 — clean but BN renders a few small artifacts):

//   2. Attempted set_function_prototype with zVec3* points — SUCCESS.
//   3. Acceptable — the eax_1/frontOld pair at 0x46c5bb is the MSVC `cdq; sub eax,edx; sar 1` rounding-toward-zero idiom.
//   4. `back = &points[pointCount] - 0xc` retains a raw -12 byte offset because BN cannot simultaneously apply zVec3* sizing to the base index AND a constant byte subtrahend. Documented by 0x46c5c3 address comment.
//   5. `frontStore` is still rendered as `float*` (not zVec3*) because the write stream uses three separate float stores (*frontStore, frontStore[1], frontStore[2]) — retyping to zVec3* would require BN to discover the aggregate store pattern; it currently keeps the element-granular view. //

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x46f690 zInput::KeyboardPollState (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Pump the keyboard DirectInput device queue and update g_zInputKbdKeyDispatchTable for one frame.
//
// Signature: void __fastcall(int8_t dispatchCallbacks). The boolean arrives in cl and is stashed in a local slot (esp+0x13 after the GetDeviceData call).
//
// Global state touched:
//   g_zInput_KbdDevice           @ 0x561cc8 -- IDirectInputDevice* (DirectInput 5/7 keyboard)
//   g_zInput_KbdEventBuffer      @ 0x561ccc -- DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA rgdod[128] working buffer
//   g_zInput_KbdModifierState    @ 0x561cd0 -- sticky modifier bitfield (ah: bit0=Alt, bit1=Ctrl, bit2=Shift)
//   g_zInputKbdKeyDispatchTable  @ 0x561cd4 -- struct zInput_KbdKeyDispatchEntry[0x7de] (2014 slots)
//   g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallback @ 0x565bc4 -- optional int32_t(__fastcall*)(int ascii, void* ctx)
//   g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallbackCtx @ 0x565bc8 -- ctx passed to the raw-event callback
//
// Dispatch table layout: each slot is indexed by (dikScanCode | (modifiers << 8)) giving the modifier-aware key-combo space used by the BindMap. Valid indices are [0..0x7de). Slot fields:
//   state      : small transition enum shared with Mouse/DI getters (0 idle, 1 held, 2 held-consumed, 4 down-edge)
//   callbackFn : int32_t (__fastcall *)(int32_t dikCodeWithMods) -- optional per-combo hot callback
//
// Flow:
//   1. Retrieve up to 128 DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA entries via g_zInput_KbdDevice->lpVtbl->GetDeviceData(this, cbObjectData=0x10, rgdod=&g_zInput_KbdEventBuffer[0], pdwInOut=&localCount{=0x80 in}, dwFlags=0) (vtable +0x28).
//      - On DIERR_INPUTLOST (0x8007001e) call Acquire() at vtable +0x1c and fall through with zero events.
//      - On any other error, route to zInput_DI_ErrorToString with error code 0x170 and the format buffer at 0x4e08cc, then return.
//
//   2. Process-loop (edi = event index 0..localCount):
//      For each DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA at esi (stride 0x10):
//        a. Branch on dwOfs via a jump table at 0x46f8ac keyed by (dwOfs - 0x1d); out-of-range goes to the generic path.
//        b. Modifier path (Alt/Ctrl/Shift keys): test dwData bit 7 (key-pressed flag), update bit 0/1/2 of g_zInput_KbdModifierState's ah byte accordingly, then jump to the shared tail.
//        c. Generic key path: if g_zInput_KbdModifierState is non-zero AND the existing slot state is non-zero, force slot state = 4 (down-edge pending) so a held modifier + new keystroke produces a fresh edge. Then copy the current modifier bits into the post-processed flag byte at dwData:
//            modBit Alt   (ah&1) -> dwData |= 0x40
//            modBit Ctrl  (ah&2) -> dwData |= 0x20
//            modBit Shift (ah&4) -> dwData |= 0x10
//          and OR the modifier bits (<<8) into the slot index for the state write-back.
//        d. Shared tail (0x46f7c2): look up the slot and update its state.
//           If dwData bit 7 (key pressed): state = (prev == 1 ? 3 : 1) via the dec/neg/sbb/and 0xfe/add 3 idiom -- held-first-frame or held-consumed.
//           Otherwise (key released): set state bit 2 (|=4), marking a down->up edge. If g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallback is non-null, call zInput_KBD_TranslateDikToAscii(dikCode) to get the ASCII value and invoke the raw callback with (ascii, g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallbackCtx).
//
//   3. If dispatchCallbacks is non-zero, second loop (ebp = event index) walks the same DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA buffer to invoke per-combo hot callbacks:

//

//

//

//

// -- end xref --

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x46f980 zInput::KeyboardGetKeyTransitionState (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Likely original file: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zInput\zin_kbd.cpp
// Consume-on-read transition-state query for a packed DIK key combo index in g_zInputKbdKeyDispatchTable. If state has bit 2 set, returns the original state and clears it to 0; if state is exactly 1, promotes the stored state to 2 while returning 1.

0x468760 int32_t __fastcall zInput::KeyboardGetKeyTransitionState(int32_t keyIndex)
{

    if ((state.b & 4) != 0)

    return state
}

// Different from Recoil.bndb.
0x4690f0 void zInput::MouseUpdateAcquireState()
{

    if (g_zInput_MouseActive == 0)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x471950 zInput::BindMapContextPop (match: exact; via exact)

// Likely original file: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zInput\zinput.cpp. Pops the current bind-map overlay, frees an overlay context when m_isOverlay is set, restores the saved context from the overlay node stack, returns the node to the free list, and rebuilds lookup tables. // Hamilton product of two unit quaternions, out = a * b:
//   w = a.w*b.w - a.x*b.x - a.y*b.y - a.z*b.z

//   y = a.w*b.y + a.y*b.w + a.z*b.x - a.x*b.z
//   z = a.w*b.z + a.z*b.w + a.x*b.y - a.y*b.x
// __fastcall: ecx=a, edx=b, stack arg=outAB. Used by zEffect::AnimateNodeOverTime to compose incremental frame rotations.
// -- end xref --
0x46e6c0 void __fastcall zMathQuatMultiply(struct zQuat const* quatA, struct zQuat const* quatB, struct zQuat* outAB)
{

    *outAB_1 = quatB->w * quatA->w - quatA->x * quatB->x - quatA->y * quatB->y - quatA->z * quatB->z
    outAB_1[1] = quatB->w * quatA->x + quatA->w * quatB->x + quatB->z * quatA->y - quatA->z * quatB->y
    outAB_1[2] = quatB->w * quatA->y + quatA->w * quatB->y + quatA->z * quatB->x - quatB->z * quatA->x

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x480d20 zModel_Material::CompareForReuse (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zModel\zModel_Matl.cpp
//
// Tests whether two zModel_Material values are equivalent for reuse.
//
// Returns 0 when reusable, non-zero (1 or +/-1 from sbb idiom) otherwise.
//
// Algorithm:
// 1. Quick-reject: if lhs->currentTextureDirectoryEntry != rhs->currentTextureDirectoryEntry, return 1.
// 2. Compare the first 32 bytes byte-for-byte via `rep cmpsb` — that covers flags, packedColor, colorRgb, currentTextureDirectoryEntry, unknown_14, unknown_18, unknown_1c (offsets 0..0x1f). // 3. If first 32 bytes match: compare userTag. Equal ⇒ return 0 (reusable). One side zero ⇒ copy the non-zero userTag into the zero slot and return 0 (in-place "tag promotion" so the cached entry inherits the caller's tag). Both non-zero and different ⇒ return 1.
//
// Note: BN's HLIL faithfully shows the `rep cmpsb` as a manual byte-by-byte loop with sbb-idiom render — the loop counter (i = 0x20) and the temp char compares are the compiler-emitted form of `memcmp(lhs, rhs, 32)`. The `bool c_1 = unimplemented {sbb eax, eax}` marker at 0x480d45 is BN's standard render of the sbb-eax-eax/sbb-eax-(-1) sign-of-difference idiom.
// -- end xref --
0x479ad0 int32_t __fastcall zModel_Material::CompareForReuse(struct zModel_Material* lhs, struct zModel_Material* rhs)
{

    if (currentTextureDirectoryEntry != rhs->currentTextureDirectoryEntry)
        return 1

    int32_t i = 0x20
    struct zModel_Material* rhs_1 = rhs
    struct zModel_Material* lhs_1 = lhs
    int32_t result = 0
    bool c = false
    bool z = currentTextureDirectoryEntry == currentTextureDirectoryEntry

    while (i != 0)
        char temp2_1 = lhs_1->flags.b
        char temp3_1 = rhs_1->flags.b
        c = temp2_1 u< temp3_1
        z = temp2_1 == temp3_1
        lhs_1 = &lhs_1->flags + 1
        rhs_1 = &rhs_1->flags + 1
        i -= 1

        if (not(z))
            break

    if (not(z))
        result = sbb.d(sbb.d(0, 0, c), 0xffffffff, c)

    if (result == 0)
        int32_t userTag = lhs->userTag
        int32_t userTag_1 = rhs->userTag

        if (userTag != userTag_1)
            if (userTag == 0)
                lhs->userTag = userTag_1
                return result

            if (userTag_1 != 0)
                return 1

            rhs->userTag = userTag

    return result
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x482080 zDi::AllocFromFreeList (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Original file: Battlesport/zModel/gmod_const.c
//
// struct zDi* __cdecl zModel_DiPool_AllocFromFreeList(void)
//
// Pop the head of the zDi free list and return a zeroed, flagged zDi slot.
//
//   1. slotIndex = g_zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex.  If negative (empty), report
//      "Creating Model3D; model buffer full" via zError::ReportOld and return 0.
//   2. entry = &g_zModel_DiPoolBase[slotIndex]  (sizeof(zDi) == 88 == 0x58).
//   3. Pop: g_zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex = entry->nextFreeIndex.
//   4. g_zModel_DiPoolInUseCount++.
//   5. memset(entry, 0, 0x54) — clear all 84 payload bytes; leave nextFreeIndex
//      intact (the FreeIfUnreferenced/relink code expects it).
//   6. entry->flags = (entry->flags & 0xDF) | 3 — flags bit0|bit1 set, bit5 clear.
//      (After the memset, flags is already 0, so this just writes 3.)
//   7. Return entry.
//
// Paired with zModel_DiPool::FreeIfUnreferenced @ 0x4820f0 which pushes back onto the free list.
//
// Note on variables:
//   - slotByteOffsetDiv8 = slotIndex * 11; the byte offset into the pool is
//     slotByteOffsetDiv8 * 8 = slotIndex * 88.  MSVC factored the multiply to
//     keep the *8 inside an x86 LEA scale factor.
//   - diPoolBase typed zModel_DiSlotLinkView* (identical 88-byte layout, but
//     exposes diPayloadWords[21] + nextFreeIndex for the free-list traversal).
// -- end xref --
0x47ae30 struct zDi* zDi::AllocFromFreeList()
{
    int32_t zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex_1 = g_zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex

    if (zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex_1 s< 0)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x482160 zDi::FreeContents (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Original file: Battlesport/zModel/gdi.c
//
// int32_t __fastcall zDi::FreeContents(zDi* self)
//
// Releases all owned allocations inside a zDi mesh container WITHOUT freeing the
// zDi struct itself.  Sequence:
//   1. If self == nullptr return 5 (error: null-receiver sentinel, same code used by
//      other zDi setters in gdi.c).
//   2. For each of self->entryCount zDiEntries: free vertexIndices, normalIndices,
//      uvPairs and null them out.
//   3. Free the entries/verts/normals/blendVerts arrays (each optional, null check
//      before free).  Null out each pointer on self.
//   4. If self->pointEntries != nullptr, walk self->pointCount pointEntries and
//      free each entry->pointCamList (optional), then free the pointEntries array.
//   5. Return 0 on success.
//
// Note on variables:
//   - entryNormIdxPtr (int32_t**) — MSVC aliased a pointer into each zDiEntry at
//     offset +12 (normalIndices).  ptr[-1] = vertexIndices (offset 8),
//     *ptr       = normalIndices (offset 12), ptr[1] = uvPairs (offset 16).
//     The loop steps ptr by +28 bytes (= sizeof(zDiEntry)).
//   - pointEntryByteOff — byte offset added to &pointEntries[0].pointCamList; stride
//     +0x4c = sizeof(zModel_PointEntry).  Equivalent to pointEntries[pointIdx].pointCamList.
//
// EXHAUSTION CHECKLIST (crit 6 + 11 ☑️ basis):
//   1. [tried] Retype entryNormIdxPtr to zDiEntry* — rejected; changes stride
//      arithmetic (&ptr[7] becomes 7*sizeof(zDiEntry) = 196 bytes), breaking loop.
//   2. [tried] Retype entryNormIdxPtr to a 3-int32_t** helper struct — BN cannot
//      express negative field offsets; dropped.
//   3. [tried] Redefine zDiEntry to center on normalIndices with negative field
//      offsets — BN struct offsets must be non-negative.
//   4. [tried] Split variable at definition to retype per-iteration — same stride
//      problem recurs on each SSA instance.
//   5. [tried] Retype pointEntryByteOff to zModel_PointEntry* — loses the byte
//      offset semantics since BN doesn't have a struct-indexed add expression
//      equivalent to the raw pointer+offset the code uses.
//   Accepted rendering: annotate SSA register vars and document aliasing via
//   address comments; C/C++ reader can see which zDiEntry/zModel_PointEntry field
//   each pointer dereference touches.
// -- end xref --

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x484250 zDi::SetCurrentVariantCycleTextureCount (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// zDi_SetCurrentVariantCycleTextureCount — set the cycle-texture frame count
// on the current zDiEntry's material slot.
//
// Forwarder/validator that walks zDi → zDiEntry → zModel_Material and forwards
// the texture count to zModel_Material_SetCycleTextureCount. NULL-zDi guard with
// debug-print error path; NULL-materialRef "fallback" is buggy (see below) but
// unreachable for any zDi loaded by the world loader.
//
// Prototype: int32_t __fastcall(struct zDi* di, int32_t textureCount)
// Size: 86 bytes, 5 basic blocks, 0x484250..0x4842a5
//
// Returns:
//    0 on success (SetCycleTextureCount called, or unreachable matRef==NULL path)
//   -1 (0xffffffff) if di == NULL (caller error; logged to stderr)
//
// Walk:
//
//   Phase 1 (0x484250..0x484252) — di NULL guard.
//     test ecx, ecx; jne block 2.
//
//   Phase 2-error (0x484254..0x48428b) — di == NULL fast path.
//     Format error message into g_zError_DebugMsgBuffer @ 0x575de0:
//       "%s(%d): ERROR setting model cycle texture. Model 3D pointer is NULL.\n"
//        "D:\\Proj\\GameZRecoil\\zModel\\gmod_const.c", line 0xf3f (3903)
//     Then fprintf(stderr, &g_zError_DebugMsgBuffer).
//     stderr is loaded as `[g__iob @ 0x4cc4f8] + 0x40` — the third FILE slot in
//     the CRT _iob array.
//     Returns -1 via `or eax, 0xffffffff`.
//
//   Phase 2-walk (0x48428c..0x484294) — Walk to materialRef.
//     ecx = di->entries           [+0x30, struct zDiEntry*]
//     ecx = entries->materialRef  [+0x14, struct zModel_Material*]
//     test/jne block 4.
//
//   Phase 3-call (0x48429e..0x4842a5) — Normal path: forward to material setter.
//     EDX still holds caller's textureCount.
//     call zModel_Material_SetCycleTextureCount(matRef=ECX, textureCount=EDX)
//     return 0.
//
//   Phase 3-bug (0x484296..0x48429d) — UNREACHABLE in practice (BUG path).
//     Reached when di->entries->materialRef == NULL. ECX is NULL at this point.
//     The instruction `and word [ecx], 0xfbff` would dereference NULL and crash
//     if ever taken. Almost certainly an original-source bug:
//       - The intent was probably "clear the cycle-texture flag on this entry/DI
//         so the renderer doesn't try to advance it." The author likely meant
//         `*(matRef-pointer-to-something-else)` but forgot to reload the pointer.
//       - In all observed game-data paths, materialRef is populated by the world
//         loader before any caller of this function sees the DI, so the path is
//         not exercised. The function's behavior on this edge would be a crash,
//         not a silent return.
//     Returns 0 if it ever did fall through (xor eax, eax; retn).
//
// CALLEES (1 conditional + 2 CRT):
//
//   zModel_Material_SetCycleTextureCount @ 0x481050  ✅  (named; verify recon)
//       The actual cycle-texture-count setter on a zModel_Material instance.
//   sprintf  (CRT, via [0x4cc5c4]) — error formatter
//   fprintf  (CRT, via [0x4cc5bc]) — stderr writer
//
// CALLERS (2 sites):
//
//   zEffect::InitFromPath              @ 0x46022c
//       Per-effect-entry initialization: after locating the zDi via
//       FindNodeUserDataRecursive, sets the texture count from the loaded
//       MAPS subnode child count.
//
//   zInterp_Context_DispatchCoreCommand @ 0x4c295a
//       Script command dispatch — the interp interpreter exposes this as a
//       runtime-tweakable command for cycle-texture parameters.
//
// Globals & data:
//   g_zError_DebugMsgBuffer @ 0x575de0 — shared scratch for error formatters
//   g__iob                  @ 0x4cc4f8 — pointer to CRT _iob[0]; +0x40 = stderr
//   &sprintf                @ 0x4cc5c4 — CRT import slot
//   &fprintf                @ 0x4cc5bc — CRT import slot
//   fmt string              @ 0x4e17b0
//   source path             @ 0x4e13a0 — "D:\\Proj\\GameZRecoil\\zModel\\gmod_const.c"
//
// Source attribution:
//   Comment in get_assembly notes "D:\\Proj\\GameZRecoil\\zModel\\zmodel.cpp"
//   for the function start, but the error message itself names gmod_const.c
//   line 3903. The function compiled into zmodel.cpp's translation unit even
//   though its diagnostic message references gmod_const.c — likely an inlined
//   header macro pattern.
//
// BN HLIL render notes:
//   - HLIL renders the buggy NULL-deref branch as
//     `materialRef->flags &= 0xfbff` even though materialRef IS NULL on that
//     path. This is BN faithfully transliterating the asm — it does not detect
//     that the dominator's branch guarantees materialRef == 0 here. Documented
//     as an original-code bug, not a render artifact.
//   - HLIL uses `_iob + 0x40` instead of `stderr`. That is the canonical
//     CRT-import idiom in this codebase; ~150 callers use the same pattern.
// -- end xref --
0x47d000 int32_t __fastcall zDi::SetCurrentVariantCycleTextureCount(struct zDi* di, int32_t textureCount)
{
    if (di == 0)
        sprintf(&g_zError_DebugMsgBuffer, "%s(%d): ERROR setting model cycle texture. Model 3D pointer is NULL.\n", "D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zModel\gmod_const.c", 0xf3f)
        fprintf(&_iob[2], &g_zError_DebugMsgBuffer)
        return 0xffffffff

    struct zModel_Material* materialRef = di->entries->materialRef

    if (materialRef != 0)
        zModel_Material::SetCycleTextureCount(materialRef, textureCount)
        return 0

    materialRef->flags &= 0xfbff
    return 0
}

        list->head = node->next

    node->prev->next = node->next
    node->next->prev = node->prev
    zArchiveListFreeNode(node)
    int32_t result = list->count - 1
    list->count = result
    return result
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x48cc20 zArchiveListFindKey (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// zArchiveList_FindPayloadByValue(zArchiveList* list, uint32_t value)
//   Locate the first payload in the list whose leading dword equals
//   `value`, and return that payload pointer (NOT the node). Returns
//   NULL when the list is empty or no match exists.
//
// ABI: __fastcall (ECX=list, EDX=value), no stack args.
//
// Algorithm:
//   1. Reject NULL list and empty list (list->count == 0).
//   2. Walk the circular doubly-linked node ring starting at list->head.
//   3. At each step, dereference node->payload and compare *(uint32_t*)
//      payload against `value`. Match -> return node->payload.
//   4. Loop terminates when the cursor wraps back to head.
//
// Layout reminders (already typed):
//   zArchiveList: count@0x00, head@0x10
//   zUtilFileIndexNode: payload@0x00, next@0x04, prev@0x08
//
// Sole caller: zEffect::AcquireRuntimeEntryByIndex @ 0x4620e5, which
// stores zEffect runtime entries with their per-entry index at the
// start of the payload struct, so this is effectively
// "find_runtime_entry_by_index" in that context. Helper lives in the
// generic zArchiveList runtime (GameZRecoil/zUtil/zutl_zar.cpp).
// -- end xref --
0x484b50 void* __fastcall zArchiveListFindKey(struct zArchiveList* list, uint32_t value)
{
    if (list != 0 && list->count != 0)
        struct zUtilFileIndexNode* head = list->head
        struct zUtilFileIndexNode* next = head

        if (*next->payload == value)
            return next->payload

        while (true)
            next = next->next

            if (next == head)
                return 0

            if (*next->payload == value)
                return next->payload

    return 0
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x48cdc0 zReader::Load (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zReader\zReader.cpp
//
// Opens a .zrd file from the given path and parses it into a fresh zReader node tree.
//
// Algorithm:
// 1. _splitpath(path, NULL, NULL, g_zReader_FileNameBuf, g_zReader_FileExtBuf) — splits path into name and extension into two separate global buffers.
// 2. Open-coded strcat: walks each buffer with `repne scasb` to find its null terminator, then memcpy-splices the extension onto the end of the filename so g_zReader_FileNameBuf becomes "name.ext".
// 3. zReader_OpenFileFromMountedArchives(g_zReader_FileNameBuf) walks every mounted index archive looking for the requested file; on success returns the (shared) archive HANDLE positioned at the file's offset.
// 4. zReader_AllocateNode(4, 1) allocates an 8-byte root node with type=ZRDR_NODE_ARRAY (4) and writes header word 4 into *result.
// 5. zReader_ReadNode(hFile, root) parses the file content into the root node tree.
// 6. Returns root (NULL if file not found in any mounted archive).
//
// The shared HANDLE means concurrent loads are unsafe — the file pointer is owned by the archive and any second OpenFileByName call repositions it.
//
// BN-render notes:
// - The two `while (i != 0) { cond = *p; ... }` loops at 0x48cde5 and 0x48cdf7 are open-coded strlen sequences (`repne scasb` with i = 0xffffffff).
// - The two `__builtin_memcpy` calls at 0x48cdff and 0x48ce06 form a single dword+tail-byte memcpy (`rep movsd; rep movsb`) appending the extension to the filename buffer in place.
// -- end xref --
0x484cf0 struct zReader_Node* __fastcall zReader::Load(char* path, int32_t reservedEdx, int32_t reservedStack)
{

    _splitpath(path, nullptr, nullptr, &g_zReader_FileNameBuf, &g_zReader_FileExtBuf)
    char* edi = &g_zReader_FileExtBuf
    int32_t i = 0xffffffff

    while (i != 0)
        bool cond:0_1 = 0 != *edi
        edi = &edi[1]
        i -= 1

        if (not(cond:0_1))
            break

    int32_t ecx = not.d(i)
    char* edi_2 = &g_zReader_FileNameBuf
    int32_t i_1 = 0xffffffff

    while (i_1 != 0)
        bool cond:1_1 = 0 != *edi_2
        edi_2 = &edi_2[1]
        i_1 -= 1

        if (not(cond:1_1))
            break

    int32_t esi_1
    int32_t edi_4
    edi_4, esi_1 = __builtin_memcpy(edi_2 - 1, edi - ecx, ecx & 0xfffffffc)
    __builtin_memcpy(edi_4, esi_1, ecx & 3)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a61b0 zIndexArchive::~zIndexArchive (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Destructor of zIndexArchive (the struct itself is owned by the caller — e.g. a stack-local in zSndSampleSet_Init or a slot inside the mount table in zArchive_MountIndexArchive):
//
//   1. zIndexArchive::CloseAndFreeRecords(self)   — flushes on dirty, closes hFile, frees records[] and resets all fields.
//   2. if (self->reservedFree != nullptr) free(self->reservedFree) — frees the auxiliary buffer that the mount/load path stashed at offset 0 (e.g. the slurped index image).
//
// reservedFree is not cleared after free(); that's fine because CloseAndFreeRecords already zeroed it via FreeRecordsAndReset before this second free runs — confirm by reading order: CloseAndFreeRecords sets reservedFree=0 in FreeRecordsAndReset's epilogue, so the subsequent test on the local copy (captured BEFORE the call into CloseAndFreeRecords via the esi live-register reuse) is the archived original value of reservedFree. This is subtle: the compiler captured self->reservedFree into esi *after* the call returned, but the original self pointer was preserved; the load happens on a now-zeroed struct. In practice this means a double free is avoided only because CloseAndFreeRecords had already nulled reservedFree; wait — re-examine.
//
// Actually the assembly is:
//   mov esi, ecx              ; esi = self
//   call CloseAndFreeRecords  ; ecx = self -- corrupts esi? No, esi is callee-saved.
//   mov esi, [esi]            ; esi = self->reservedFree  -- AFTER the call, so AFTER FreeRecordsAndReset zeroed it
//
// So the test always sees 0 here and the free is unreachable at runtime when the archive was ever opened. The branch exists for the uninitialized-slot path, where FreeRecordsAndReset's early-return (records==0) skips the field-zeroing and reservedFree is whatever the caller left it.
//
// Specifically: FreeRecordsAndReset returns early if records==nullptr WITHOUT zeroing reservedFree. So if the archive was never successfully loaded (records stayed null but reservedFree got pre-allocated by a partial init), Destroy still frees that allocation. This is the safety net.
//
// Callers: zArchive_MountIndexArchive, zUtil_ZRDR_UnloadMountedArchives, zSndSampleSet_Init (error paths), zZbdManager::Destroy, and SEH thunk sub_4cb140.
// -- end xref --
0x49e240 void __fastcall zIndexArchive::~zIndexArchive(struct zIndexArchive* self)
{
    zIndexArchive::CloseAndFreeRecords(self)
    void* reservedFree = self->reservedFree

    if (reservedFree != 0)
        free(reservedFree)
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a61d0 zIndexArchive::Init (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp (line 76 matches the error-report call site).
//
// Open a .zar archive for read and load its index table into memory.
//
// Assumes the caller has already zeroed the zIndexArchive struct (e.g. via zIndexArchive::Reset or stack-zero-init). Only writes self->hFile directly; the rest of the struct is populated by LoadIndexFromTail -> EnsureCapacity.
//
// Sequence:
//   hFile = CreateFileA(filepath,
//                       GENERIC_READ,
//                       FILE_SHARE_READ,
//                       NULL,
//                       OPEN_EXISTING,
//                       FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL | FILE_FLAG_RANDOM_ACCESS,  -- 0x80 | 0x10000000 = 0x10000080
//                       NULL);
//   self->hFile = hFile;
//   if (hFile != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
//       return zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail(self);
//   // failure path
//   dwErr = GetLastError();
//   FormatMessageA(FORMAT_MESSAGE_ALLOCATE_BUFFER | FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM,  -- 0x1100
//                  NULL, dwErr, LANG_NEUTRAL|SUBLANG_NEUTRAL (0x400),
//                  &msgBuf, 0, NULL);
//   zError::ReportOld(0x400, "zutl_zar.cpp", 76, "GetLastError(0x%08x): %s", dwErr, msgBuf);
//   LocalFree(msgBuf);
//   return 0;
//
// NOTE: the compiler reuses the incoming `filepath` stack slot as the storage for msgBuf (the FormatMessage-allocated buffer pointer), because `filepath` was captured into eax before CreateFileA and is no longer needed. BN therefore renders the failure path as `FormatMessageA(..., &filepath, ...)` and `LocalFree(filepath)`, but the value in that slot has been overwritten with the allocated message-buffer pointer. This is purely a decompiler-naming artifact; behavior is correct.
//
// Returns: BOOL — 1 if file opened AND tail index parsed successfully, 0 otherwise.
// -- end xref --
0x49e260 int32_t __thiscall zIndexArchive::Init(struct zIndexArchive* self, char* filepath)
{
    HANDLE eax = CreateFileA(filepath, 0x80000000, FILE_SHARE_READ, nullptr, OPEN_EXISTING, 0x10000080, nullptr)
    int32_t result = 0
    result.b = eax != 0xffffffff
    self->hFile = eax

    if (result != 0)
        return zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail(self)

    FormatMessageA(FORMAT_MESSAGE_ALLOCATE_BUFFER | FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM, nullptr, GetLastError(), 0x400, &filepath, 0, nullptr)
    LocalFree(filepath)
    return result
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a62b0 zIndexArchive::CloseAndFreeRecords (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Close an open zIndexArchive, flushing any pending changes to disk, and reset all members to their empty/closed state.
//
// Sequence:
//   1. If self->dirty != 0, call zIndexArchive::FlushIndexToTail(self) which appends records+trailer to the file.
//   2. If self->hFile != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, CloseHandle(self->hFile).
//   3. self->hFile = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE (the redundant clear before FreeRecordsAndReset is an explicit guard against reuse after step 2).
//   4. zIndexArchive::FreeRecordsAndReset(self) — free() records[] if non-null and zero every field.
//
// Returns BOOL/1 unconditionally — callers (zUtil_ZRDR_UnloadMountedArchives, zSndSampleSet_Init, zIndexArchive::Destroy, zZbdManager::LoadEntries/LoadZarFile) treat the return as always-success.
// -- end xref --
0x49e340 int32_t __fastcall zIndexArchive::CloseAndFreeRecords(struct zIndexArchive* self)
{
    if (self->dirty != 0)
        zIndexArchive::FlushIndexToTail(self)

    HANDLE hFile = self->hFile

    if (hFile != 0xffffffff)
        CloseHandle(hFile)

    self->hFile = 0xffffffff
    zIndexArchive::FreeRecordsAndReset(self)
    return 1
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a62f0 zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Grow self->records[] to hold at least requiredCount zZarFileRecord entries.
//
// Algorithm (standard grow-by-2 dynamic array):
//   if (requiredCount < recordCapacity) return;        // already big enough (note: strict <, so capacity == requiredCount still grows)
//   newCapacity = max(recordCapacity * 2, requiredCount + 1);
//   self->recordCapacity = newCapacity;
//   self->records = realloc(self->records, newCapacity * sizeof(zZarFileRecord));  // sizeof=0x94
//
// Notes:
//   - Initial call with recordCapacity=0 picks branch requiredCount+1 (since 2*0==0 <= requiredCount+1).
//   - realloc(NULL, size) is equivalent to malloc(size), which is the path hit on the first call from zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail.
//   - Return value of realloc is stored unchecked — OOM would null self->records and subsequent access would crash; the engine treats allocation failure as fatal.
//   - Byte-count formula: edx = eax + 4*(9*eax) = 37*eax, then <<2 = 148*eax = 0x94*eax.
//   - recordCount is unchanged; only capacity grows.
//   - Callers: zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail, zIndexArchive::AddFileRecord.
// -- end xref --
0x49e380 void __thiscall zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity(struct zIndexArchive* self, int32_t requiredCount)
{
    int32_t recordCapacity = self->recordCapacity

    if (requiredCount u< recordCapacity)
        return

    int32_t eax = recordCapacity * 2

    if (eax u<= requiredCount + 1)
        eax = requiredCount + 1

    self->recordCapacity = eax
    self->records = realloc(self->records, eax * 0x94)
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a6330 zIndexArchive::FreeRecordsAndReset (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// If self->records != nullptr, free() it, then reset the entire zIndexArchive to a closed/empty state:
//   reservedFree = 0
//   hFile        = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE (-1)
//   recordCapacity = 0
//   recordCount    = 0
//   records        = nullptr
//   dirty          = 0
//
// If records was already null, returns immediately without touching any fields.
// -- end xref --
0x49e3c0 void __fastcall zIndexArchive::FreeRecordsAndReset(struct zIndexArchive* self)
{
    struct zZarFileRecord* records = self->records

    if (records != 0)
        free(records)
        *self = struct zIndexArchive {
            .reservedFree = 0
            .hFile = 0xffffffff
            .recordCapacity = 0
            .recordCount = 0
            .records = nullptr
            .dirty = 0
        }
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a6360 zIndexArchive::FlushIndexToTail (match: high; via callee)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Append the in-memory zZarFileRecord table to EOF of self->hFile and write the 8-byte trailer, so the archive file layout becomes:
//   [<file data>...][records[recordCount] (recordCount*0x94 bytes)][uint32 magic=1][uint32 recordCount]
//
// Step by step:
//   SetFilePointer(hFile, 0, NULL, FILE_END)           -- seek to end
//   WriteFile(hFile, self->records, recordCount*0x94, &bytesWritten, NULL)  -- records (sizeof(zZarFileRecord)=0x94)
//   WriteFile(hFile, &magic=1,         4, &bytesWritten, NULL)               -- trailer magic
//   WriteFile(hFile, &self->recordCount, 4, &bytesWritten, NULL)             -- trailer recordCount
//   self->dirty = 0
//
// Byte-count formula in assembly: edi = recordCount + 4*(9*recordCount) = 37*recordCount, then <<2 = 148*recordCount = 0x94*recordCount (= recordCount * sizeof(zZarFileRecord)).
//
// Note: return values from SetFilePointer/WriteFile are ignored; no error checking.
// -- end xref --
// Different from Recoil.bndb.
0x49e3f0 void __fastcall zIndexArchive::FlushIndexToTail(struct zIndexArchive* self)
{
    int32_t recordCount = self->recordCount
    HANDLE hFile = self->hFile
    uint32_t numberOfBytesWritten = 0
    int32_t buffer = 1
    SetFilePointer(hFile, 0, nullptr, FILE_END)
    WriteFile(self->hFile, self->records, recordCount * 0x94, &numberOfBytesWritten, nullptr)
    WriteFile(self->hFile, &buffer, 4, &numberOfBytesWritten, nullptr)
    WriteFile(self->hFile, &self->recordCount, 4, &numberOfBytesWritten, nullptr)
    self->dirty = 0
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a63f0 zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Parse the trailer of the already-open self->hFile and load the zZarFileRecord index table into memory.
//
// On-disk layout (written by zIndexArchive::FlushIndexToTail):
//   [<raw file data>...]
//   [records[recordCount]  (recordCount * sizeof(zZarFileRecord) = recordCount * 0x94 bytes)]
//   [uint32_t magic=1]        // 4 bytes
//   [uint32_t recordCount]    // 4 bytes
//   <-- EOF
//
// Algorithm:
//   1. size = GetFileSize(hFile); if (size < 8) return 0;              // too small to hold trailer
//   2. Seek EOF-8 (FILE_END, -8).
//   3. Read 4 bytes -> footerMagic
//   4. Read 4 bytes -> recordCountFromTail
//   5. if (footerMagic != 1) return 0;                                 // not a valid zIndexArchive
//   6. zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity(self, recordCountFromTail)        // grow records[] to fit
//   7. Seek EOF-(8 + recordCountFromTail*0x94) (FILE_END).
//   8. Read recordCountFromTail*0x94 bytes into self->records.
//   9. Seek 0 (FILE_BEGIN)                                             // restore for subsequent zReader reads
//  10. self->recordCount = recordCountFromTail
//  11. return 1
//
// Return values of ReadFile/SetFilePointer are not checked — if a partial read happens the records array is trusted to have been filled.
//
// Byte-count formula: edi = eax + 4*(9*eax) = 37*eax, then <<2 = 148*eax = 0x94*eax, matching FlushIndexToTail.
// -- end xref --
0x49e480 int32_t __thiscall zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail(struct zIndexArchive* self)
{
    if (GetFileSize(self->hFile, nullptr) u< 8)
        return 0

    SetFilePointer(self->hFile, 0xfffffff8, nullptr, FILE_END)
    uint32_t numberOfBytesRead
    int32_t buffer
    ReadFile(self->hFile, &buffer, 4, &numberOfBytesRead, nullptr)
    int32_t var_c
    ReadFile(self->hFile, &var_c, 4, &numberOfBytesRead, nullptr)

    if (buffer != 1)
        return 0

    zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity(self, var_c)
    int32_t nNumberOfBytesToRead = var_c * 0x94
    SetFilePointer(self->hFile, 0xfffffff8 - nNumberOfBytesToRead, nullptr, FILE_END)
    ReadFile(self->hFile, self->records, nNumberOfBytesToRead, &numberOfBytesRead, nullptr)
    SetFilePointer(self->hFile, 0, nullptr, FILE_BEGIN)
    self->recordCount = var_c
    return 1
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a64d0 zIndexArchive::AddFileRecord (match: high; via callee)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a6670 zIndexArchive::ReadFileByName (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Likely original file: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp
// Finds a case-insensitive record by name, publishes record->fileSize through *bufferSize, returns 0x10001 if absent, 0x10002 if the caller buffer is too small, or 0 after seeking and reading the payload. // -- end xref --
0x49e6f0 int32_t __thiscall zIndexArchive::ReadFileByName(struct zIndexArchive* self, char* filename, void* buffer, int32_t* bufferSize)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4a6840 zVideo::RunPostprocessOnPrimaryBuffer (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Runs the FxPass3 postprocess pipeline against the engine's primary surface and queues a primitive for it.
//
// Lock gate (run only if either condition is met):

//   || g_zVideo_UseHalfResBackbuffer (@ 0x632128) != 0                    -- software half-res mode also locks

//

//
// Returns void (xor eax,eax). Calling convention: __cdecl, no args, balanced stack. Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zVideo\zVideo.cpp.
// -- end xref --
0x49e8c0 void zVideo::RunPostprocessOnPrimaryBuffer()
{

    zRndr::SetFrameBufferRegion(g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pixels, nullptr, 0, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pitch)
    zVideo::FxSetSurfaceState(g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pixels, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.width, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.height, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pitch)
    zVideo::FxPass3QueuePrimitive(g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pixels, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.width, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.height, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pitch)

    if (g_zVideo_UseHalfResBackbuffer != 0)

// -- end xref --
0x4a5690 int32_t __fastcall zVideo_dd3d::FloorPowerOfTwo(int32_t value) __pure
{

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4ae380 OptCatalog::BlendDirectionTowardTarget (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Physical source-file block candidate: src/GameZRecoil/zWeapon/zwep_init.c [0x4ae380, 0x4b2960). Evidence: source-path literal 0x4e45d8 xref(s) not listed in handoff; medium-low, broad OptCatalog/zWeapon source-block candidate. Use docs/reconstruction/source_file_layout_audit.md; not an owner/tier gate by itself.
// -- end xref --
0x4a6390 void __fastcall OptCatalog::BlendDirectionTowardTarget(struct zVec3* direction, struct zVec3* targetDirection, float xWeight, float yWeight, float zWeight)
{
    direction->x = (targetDirection->x - direction->x) * xWeight + direction->x
    direction->y = (targetDirection->y - direction->y) * yWeight + direction->y
    direction->z = (targetDirection->z - direction->z) * zWeight + direction->z
    zMath::Vec3Normalize(direction)
}

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4b2960 zGame::OptionsLoadFromRegistry (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Pulls staged zOptionEntry values back out of the Windows registry, overwriting their in-memory payloads.
//
// LIKELY SOURCE: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zGame\zgame_opt.c
//
// BN 5.2 still renders the dynamic alloca/strlen/memcpy path construction as compiler-lowered HLIL; the assembly/commented path map is authoritative for that prologue.
//
// --- PATH COMPOSITION (alloca'd stack buffer, rounded up to DWORD) ---

//   [ebx+4] = *0x4e4670  ("WARE")
//   [ebx+8] = *0x4e4674  ("\\\0")  <-- 2 bytes, terminates "SOFTWARE\\"

// strlen+memcpy idiom used in Save.
// Final string: `SOFTWARE\<RegKeyRoot>\<RegKeyCurrentUser>\<RegKeyGame>`.
//
// --- KEY OPENING (KEY_READ, samDesired=0x20019) ---
//   [ebp-0x8]  = HKCU handle  <- RegOpenKeyExA(HKEY_CURRENT_USER  =0x80000001)
//   [ebp-0xc]  = HKLM handle  <- RegOpenKeyExA(HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE =0x80000002)
//
// If HKCU open fails: return 0 (no close; handle was never opened).
// If HKLM open fails: close HKCU, return 0.
//
// --- ENTRY WALK ---
// For each entry on g_zGame_Options_OptionListHead (->next at +0x18):
//   registryScope := entry->registryScope (+0x14)
//     == 1  -> ebx = &HKCU_handle ([ebp-0x8])

// table at 0x4b2bc4. Unlike Save, the expected sizes are HARDCODED

//     slot 0 (INLINE_DWORD), slot 1 (INLINE_BINARY4)
//         -> expectedSize = 4, lpData = entry         (writes entry +0x00)
//     slot 2 (INLINE_BINARY8)
//         -> expectedSize = 8, lpData = entry         (writes entry +0x00..+0x07)
//     slot 3..7 (STRING_BUFFER, HEAP_BUFFER_VARIANT*, HEAP_BUFFER)
//         -> expectedSize = entry->dataSize (+0x0c)
//            lpData       = entry->heapPayload (*+0x00)
//
// --- TWO-STEP QUERY IDIOM ---
//   1. RegQueryValueExA(*ebx, entry->name, 0, &lpType, NULL, &lpcbData)
//      - Probes actual stored type and size without reading data.
//      - Non-zero result -> skip entry (missing value is non-fatal).

//   3. RegQueryValueExA(*ebx, entry->name, 0, &lpType, lpData, &expectedSize)

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4b2bf0 zGame::OptionsSaveToRegistry (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Flushes the staged zOptionEntry list back to the Windows registry.
//
// LIKELY SOURCE: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zGame\zgame_opt.c
//
// --- PATH COMPOSITION (alloca'd stack buffer, rounded up to DWORD) ---
// Builds `SOFTWARE\<RegKeyRoot>\<RegKeyCurrentUser>\<RegKeyGame>` via five
// inline strlen+memcpy+memcpy steps (compiler-lowered strcpy/strcat idiom,
// not unresolved option semantics):
//   1. "SOFTWARE\\" literal                (*g_zGame_Options_RegKeyVersionSegment @ 0x4e4668)
//   2. + g_zGame_Options_RegKeyRoot        (0x56bcd8, strdup'd by Options_InitRegistryContext)
//   3. + "\\" literal                       (at 0x4e4678)
//   4. + g_zGame_Options_RegKeyCurrentUser (0x56bcdc)
//   5. + "\\"
//   6. + g_zGame_Options_RegKeyGame        (0x56bce0)
// Total alloca = sum(strlens) + 5 + 3, ANDed with ~3 (DWORD align).
//
// --- KEY CREATION ---
// Two parallel subkeys are opened KEY_WRITE (samDesired=0x20006) with
// REG_OPTION_RESERVED, no security descriptor, no class name:
//   [ebp-0x4] = HKCU handle  <- RegCreateKeyExA(HKEY_CURRENT_USER  =0x80000001)
//   [ebp-0x8] = HKLM handle  <- RegCreateKeyExA(HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE =0x80000002)
//   [ebp-0xc] = lpdwDisposition (shared, result discarded)
//
// If HKCU create fails: closes [ebp-0x4] (invalid handle -- matches source
// binary behaviour; RegCloseKey on the zero-filled cell is a no-op/harmless
// on NT) and returns 0.
// If HKLM create fails: closes BOTH keys and returns 0.
//
// --- ENTRY WALK ---
// For each entry on g_zGame_Options_OptionListHead (->next at +0x18):
//   registryScope := entry->registryScope (+0x14)
//     == 1  -> target = &HKCU_handle ([ebp-0x4])
//     == 0  -> target = &HKLM_handle ([ebp-0x8])
//     else  -> skip entry (advance via +0x18)
//

//                          cbData  = entry->dataSize (+0x0c, caller-supplied)
//
//   Call: RegSetValueExA(*target, entry->name, 0, dwType, lpData, cbData)
//   If non-zero (failure): returns 0 immediately, WITHOUT closing either
//   registry handle (latent handle leak in failure path; matches binary).
//
// --- SUCCESS TAIL ---
// After walking to list end, closes BOTH keys (HKCU first, HKLM second,
// both via hoisted-IAT esi = RegCloseKey @ 0x4cc004) and returns 1.
//
// --- IAT SLOTS ---

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4bc320 HudUiCompositePanelEntry::ConstructorCopyRange (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Likely original file: D:\Proj\Battlesport\HudUiCompositePanel.cpp
//
// HudUiCompositePanelEntry range copy-construct (std::uninitialized_copy-style): given [sourceBegin, sourceEnd) and a destination begin pointer, copies each entry (sizeof = 0x2C0 = 704) by delegating HudUiPanel sub-object to HudUiPanel::ConstructorCopy then member-wise duplicating the 7 embedded HudUiFlash fields (flashCountdown..flashDirectionSign at offsets 0x2A4..0x2BC). //
// Calling convention is __fastcall (sourceBegin=ecx, sourceEnd=edx, destBegin=stack[0]); callee-cleans via `retn 4`. Compiler lifted the `source += 0x2C0` increment ahead of the last six field reads so the loads use short disp8 encodings (`[esi-0x18]`..`[esi-0x04]`). The split local `source` was retyped to `char*` to let BN fold those negative displacements back into direct `sourceBegin->flash.<field>` accesses instead of `__offset(-X)` artifacts. The loop still advances source by 0x2C0 per iteration in assembly; HLIL renders an outer if-guard + do-while because BN's SSA-split loses the loop PHI that would re-express the source cursor across backedges.
// -- end xref --
0x4b4280 struct HudUiCompositePanelEntry* __fastcall HudUiCompositePanelEntry::ConstructorCopyRange(struct HudUiCompositePanelEntry const* sourceBegin, struct HudUiCompositePanelEntry const* sourceEnd, struct HudUiCompositePanelEntry* destBegin)
{

    struct HudUiCompositePanelEntry* result = destBegin

    while (source != sourceEnd)
        HudUiPanel::CopyConstructor(result, source)
        float flashCountdown = source->base.base.flash.flashCountdown
        source = &source[1]
        result->base.base.flash.flashCountdown = flashCountdown
        result->base.base.flash.flashResetValue = source->__offset(0xffffffffffffffe8).d
        result->base.base.flash.flashAltColor0 = source->__offset(0xffffffffffffffec).d
        result->base.base.flash.flashAltColor1 = source->__offset(0xfffffffffffffff0).d
        result->base.base.flash.flashEnabled = source->__offset(0xfffffffffffffff4).d
        result->base.base.flash.flashMode = source->__offset(0xfffffffffffffff8).d
        result->base.base.flash.flashDirectionSign = source->base.base.vtbl:-4.d

}

//
// zTimedTask::RunImmediateAction — executes the queued immediate-mode draw action
// carried by this zTimedTask node. Dispatches on self->kind through the 8-entry
// jump table at 0x4bd640 (case = kind - 1); unknown kinds fall through to the

//
// Per-kind mapping (kind value at self->kind, args in the actionArg0..actionArg4

//

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4bd660 zTimedTask::TickActiveList (match: exact; via exact)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Source file: D:\Proj\Battlesport\hud.cpp
// Advances every task on g_zTimedTask_ActiveHead one frame, runs queued immediate draw passes, decrements deadline timers, and removes expired tasks after stamping kind=9.
// Flags: 0x01 has deadline, 0x02 skips pass 1, 0x04 runs one-shot pass 2 then clears, 0x08 runs one-shot pass 3 then clears. Pass 2 and pass 3 are mutually exclusive in one tick because the skip-pass-1 branch checks them in sequence.

// -- end xref --

// [xref] Recoil.bndb 0x4c0370 zZbdManager::LoadEntries (match: high; via callee)
// Notes below are copied from Recoil.bndb; any addresses in them are Recoil.bndb addresses.
// Opens a ZBD archive, sorts the manager's registered section handlers,
// and drives each handler's PreLoad callback so every handler can prepare
// its in-memory state from the index archive contents.
//
// --- CALLING CONVENTION ---
// __thiscall: ecx = zZbdManager* self, stack = char* filename.
// `retn 0x4` cleans up the 1 stack arg. Returns 0 on any failure, 1 on
// full success.
//
// --- STRUCT FIELD LAYOUT CONFIRMED ---
// struct zZbdManager (partial):
//   +0x04  zZbdSectionHandlerNode* sectionHandlerListSentinel
//          (ring-linked via Node::next at +0x0, Node::prev at +0x4,
//           Node::sectionHandler payload at +0x8)
//   +0x0c  zIndexArchive  archive              (embedded, NOT pointer)
//
// --- FLOW ---
// 1. Open/create the backing archive: zIndexArchive::OpenCreateWrite(
//      &self->archive, filename). Returns truthy on success, 0 on failure.
//    - On failure: ebx (i) stays 0, jump past the handler walk, return 0.
//    - On success: set ebx = 1 and continue.
//
// 2. Sort the section-handler list in ascending sortOrder:
//      zZbdManager::SortSectionHandlers(self)   (0x4c07d0)
//    This guarantees deterministic handler ordering during the preload
//    fan-out so later handlers can rely on earlier handlers' state.
//
// 3. Iterate the sorted handler ring (while node != sentinel AND i != 0):
//      Build stack context `ctx = { zZbdManager* mgr=self,
//                                   zZbdSectionHandler* handler=&node->sectionHandler }`
//      Invoke: zZbdSectionHandler::InvokePreLoad(
//                 &node->sectionHandler,   // ecx (this)
//                 &ctx)                    // stack arg
//      i = return value (0 = abort, non-zero = continue).
//      node = node->next.
//    Loop exits when either the ring is fully traversed or a handler
//    returned 0 (PreLoad veto).
//
// 4. Always close the archive:
//      zIndexArchive::CloseAndFreeRecords(&self->archive)
//    Runs on both success and handler-veto paths; only skipped when
//    OpenCreateWrite itself failed in step 1 (nothing to close).
//
// 5. Return i (ebx): 1 on full load success, 0 on open failure or handler
//    veto.
